title: Expected child error bound
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one vector and is orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\pi$. Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and choose a coordinate $i\in A$ and a family of decision trees $(T_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}$ on the remaining coordinates. For any function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, the $\pi$-average of the error probabilities of the trees $T_\omega$ is at most the error probability of the tree that queries $i$ and then uses $T_\omega$, plus half the product influence of $f$ at coordinate $i$.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$\iota$ is finite, nonempty, and has decidable equality
$B$ is a real basis of functions on $\Omega$
$B$ is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
$A$ is a set of coordinates in $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$
Each $T_\omega$ is a decision tree on the coordinates remaining after removing $i$
